title: Harris County Approves $2.5M for Independent Probe of ICE Salgado Araujo Shooting
excerpt: Harris County commissioners unanimously approved $2.5 million for the District Attorney's independent investigation into the July 7 fatal ICE shooting of Lorenzo Salgado Araujo. The DA cited unprecedented federal non-cooperation—ICE had not identified the shooting agent more than four weeks after the incident.
content:
On August 6, 2026, Harris County Commissioners Court unanimously approved $2.5 million for the District Attorney's Office to fund an independent investigation into the July 7 ICE shooting death of Lorenzo Salgado Araujo—a Houston homebuilder who was not the intended target of the enforcement operation.

District Attorney Sean Teare stated that federal authorities had initially refused to collaborate with his office, describing the lack of cooperation as "unacceptable and unprecedented." More than four weeks after the shooting, ICE had still not publicly identified the agent who fired the weapon.

  • Teare said the funds—spread over three years—could be used for additional personnel, overtime, or outside counsel, depending on investigative needs.
  • The FBI and the Texas Rangers were conducting parallel investigations.
  • The DHS OIG was also said to be leading its own independent investigation into the shooting.
  • Witnesses in the van submitted court filings suggesting an agent switched firearms after the shooting—an allegation under active investigation.
  • The shooting drew widespread protests in Houston and national calls for body cameras and accountability reforms at ICE.
